transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

My mind just won’t stop going over everything that could go wrong at work, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off anymore. It feels like I'm constantly waiting for something to fall apart, and I just don't know how to make it quiet down.
How long have you been dealing with this constant worry? Also, did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change at your work?

It’s been going on for a little over a year now. It started after I was promoted to lead our library's digital preservation and oral history initiative about a year and a half ago. That role brought on a lot of new responsibilities, tight grant deadlines, and high expectations that seemed to trigger all of this.
Do you find yourself worrying about other areas of your life as well, such as your family, health, or daily chores, or is this worry strictly focused on your work?

It definitely isn't just focused on work anymore. Even when I'm trying to relax in my garden on the weekends, my mind will start fretting about other things, like whether I've ruined my nieces' future college options because I didn't save enough money for them this year.
Along with this constant worry, have you also been experiencing a persistently low, sad mood, or a loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy, like gardening?

It’s not so much that I feel sad or depressed, but the intense anxiety and constant worry are keeping me from enjoying anything. Even when I'm in my garden, my mind is just racing with work-related 'what-ifs.' Because of that, I’ve stopped doing yoga, hiking, reading, embroidery, and going to potlucks because I’m either too keyed up or feel I have to stay home and double-check my work.
Along with feeling keyed up, have you been experiencing other physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling easily tired, or having trouble sleeping?

Yes, definitely. My shoulders and neck feel like concrete by the end of the day, and I clench my jaw so hard that it causes headaches. I also lie awake until one or two in the morning replaying work scenarios, only to wake up at 4 a.m. with my mind already racing.
Along with the muscle tension and sleep issues, have you noticed feeling easily fatigued during the day, or having trouble concentrating because your mind is so occupied with worry?

I do feel completely exhausted from the lack of sleep, but my ability to concentrate has really suffered. When I try to catalog recordings or read, my mind just drifts off into planning backup servers or rehearsing explanations for the community board. Sometimes in meetings, my mind will even go completely blank mid-sentence and I'll forget what I was saying.
Do you have any medical conditions, like thyroid issues, or are you taking any medications or consuming a lot of caffeine that might be contributing to these symptoms?

No, I don't have any known medical conditions like thyroid issues, and I'm not taking any regular medications. I also don't consume an unusual amount of caffeine, just my usual cup of coffee in the morning.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (ICD-10 F41.1). She describes persistent, generalized, and uncontrollable worry concerning multiple areas of life (work responsibilities, family finances) that has lasted for over a year. This worry is accompanied by prominent symptoms of motor tension (severe neck/shoulder stiffness, jaw clenching, headaches), apprehensive expectation (difficulty concentrating, mind going blank), and somatic symptoms (sleep initiation/maintenance insomnia, daytime fatigue). The symptoms cause significant functional impairment, leading her to withdraw from hobbies and social activities, and are not due to organic causes or substance use.
